presentation.label: HORIZON
presentation.summary: A huge, spacey reverb: eight long, slowly moving lines, from a room to a cathedral, a minute-long tail and a hold, a swell that blooms each note in.
presentation.overview: A huge, spacey reverb: eight long, slowly moving lines, from a room to a cathedral, a minute-long tail and a hold, a swell that blooms each note in.
highlights: Send a short pulse and then a sustained chord. Listen to the reverb tail for crackles.
usage: Add Horizon from the Delay group to a spare patch.
Send a short pulse and then a sustained chord. Listen to the reverb tail for crackles.
Use the page buttons to reach the remaining controls.

access.location: Delay group in the MS-70CDR effect list, under Horizon.
steps: Add Horizon from the Delay group to a spare patch.
Send a short pulse and then a sustained chord. Listen to the reverb tail for crackles.

controls.name: Size
controls.doc: params[5]. The space, a room to a cathedral (the delay lines x0.35 .. x1.52); turning it bends the pitch of the tail. Range 0–100.

controls.name: Decay
controls.doc: params[6]. Reverb time, about 0.8 s to a minute; 100 holds the tail forever and stops taking new sound. Range 0–100.

controls.name: Mod
controls.doc: params[8]. Slow movement of the delay lines: chorus in the tail, shimmer at the top. Range 0–100.

controls.name: Lo
controls.doc: params[9]. Low cut inside the tail, 20 .. 600 Hz. Range 0–100.

controls.name: Hi
controls.doc: params[10]. High cut inside the tail, 1.5 .. 16 kHz: dark to bright. Range 0–100.

controls.name: Swell
controls.doc: params[11]. Each note blooms into the reverb, over up to 2 s; 0 off. Range 0–100.

controls.name: Width
controls.doc: params[12]. Stereo width of the tail, mono .. extra wide. Range 0–100.

limitations: Hardware untested on the original MS-70CDR with OS 2.10.
